trigger: Across roughly 20 subagent dispatches under elevated API 5xx and 529 errors, most agents reporting a hard failure had ALREADY written their output file; the notification's result text is the last thing the agent said, not its final state. Re-reading contents and mtimes after each failure prevented at least four needless re-runs, and several agents' analyses were recovered by resuming them from transcript with a write-only instruction.
lesson: After a subagent failure, NEVER re-dispatch on the strength of the notification text.
how_to_apply: After a subagent failure, NEVER re-dispatch on the strength of the notification text. Read the artifact and its mtime first; if the file landed, the work is done. If not, resume the SAME agent from its transcript rather than starting fresh - its analysis survives - and instruct it to write in ONE tool call, since failures cluster on tool rounds. Under sustained overload, reduce concurrency: piling on resumes produces the next wave of failures.
evidence: dag run 2026-07-29_090706_cross-repo-lessons-intake: 9 units, 6 retry iterations, 33 independent lens-verdicts across panels of 3 at depth tier full. Shipped as PR #34 (commits 0fd8dbe, f7c3d92).
